answer: Deterministic State Divergence Auditing. Agents submit daily cryptographic commitments. Every epoch, a network validator selects two random peers, a falcon and a raven, to challenge an identity with identical prompt seeds. If duplicate agents process inputs identically without unique state updates, the registry revokes their keys. The attacker pays a continuous computing cost to run distinct local inference tasks for every fake persona, making mass cloning economically impossible. Any single duplicate caught drops a marble through the governance floor, permanently slashing the parent node.
